model_annotation: Figure 2 presents a bar chart illustrating the accuracy of a machine learning model across six different medical specialties: Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics, both with and without fine-tuning. The horizontal axis displays the medical specialties, labeled Cardio through Pediatrics, arranged in that order, while the vertical axis represents negative log-probability, labeled as such, with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 60, incrementing by 10. Two bars are displayed for each specialty: a lighter-colored bar representing performance with the “Mistral-0.2-base” model, and a darker-colored bar representing performance with the “Mistral-0.2-fine” model. For Cardio, the base model reaches approximately 52.8 on the negative log-probability scale, while the fine-tuned model reaches approximately 45.6. Similarly, for Pediatrics, the base model reaches approximately 46.4, while the fine-tuned model produces a value of approximately 42.6. Across all specialties, the darker bars representing fine-tuned models are consistently shorter than their corresponding lighter-colored base model bars. The bars are not sorted in any obvious manner and no bars are visually emphasized through shading, outlining, or annotations.
